title: Knotted pearl stitch
subtitle: A raised beaded ridge formed by evenly spaced knots on a laid thread
excerpt: Knotted pearl stitch builds a firm, beaded line by locking small raised knots at regular intervals along a foundation thread laid on the fabric surface. The knots do not pierce the fabric at each interval; they wrap around the laid thread and pull up into a rounded bead. The result is a pronounced ridged outline with a string-of-pearls quality.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), knotted stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), pearl stitch and knotted stitch entries. Note: sources use 'pearl stitch' and 'knotted stitch' as variant names for this technique; the exact working method varies slightly between authors.

content.text: Knotted pearl stitch works along a drawn line by first laying a foundation thread along that line, then wrapping and knotting the working thread around it at measured intervals. The knots sit above the laid thread and give the line its raised, beaded look. A milliner's needle with a long, uniform shaft helps the wraps slide off cleanly when each knot is pulled tight.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Perle 8 or 3 strands of stranded cotton; a heavier thread for the laid foundation and a finer working thread give the crispest beads

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Closely woven linen or cotton; loose weave will not hold the laid thread taut

items.label: Needle
items.value: Milliner's needle size 3 to 5 for the working thread; the uniform shaft is important for sliding wraps off cleanly

items.label: Hoop
items.value: 15 cm embroidery hoop; firm tension makes knot-forming easier

content.text: Secure the foundation thread on the back and bring it up at (A), the right-hand end of the line. Lay it flat along the drawn line to the left. Hold or pin the far end at (B) temporarily; it will be secured once the knots are complete.

Secure the working thread on the back and bring it up at (A), close beside the foundation thread. Slide the needle under the foundation thread from right to left at the first knot position, without picking up any fabric.

Loop the working thread over the top of the needle from left to right, then bring it under the needle tip from right to left. The thread forms a half-hitch around the needle, with the foundation thread sitting inside the loop.

Draw the needle through the loop steadily. Guide the knot down with your thumbnail as you pull so it seats firmly around the foundation thread and makes a raised bead. Do not pierce the fabric at this step.

Move along the foundation thread to the next knot position and repeat from step 2. Keep the spacing consistent. Aim for knots that touch or sit fractionally apart for a full bead effect, or space them wider for an open, dotted line.
When all knots are in place, take the foundation thread to the back at (B) and secure it. Take the working thread to the back and secure it in the same way.

attrs.heading: When knotted pearl stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The knots slide along the foundation thread instead of holding position
items.cause: The half-hitch loop was not fully seated before the next knot was started, or the foundation thread is too slippery.
items.fix: Press each knot into position with a thumbnail as you pull through. If the foundation thread is very smooth (such as silk), try a cotton perle instead; the slight texture grips the knot.

items.symptom: The beads look uneven in size or height
items.cause: Variable tension when pulling the half-hitch tight, or inconsistent spacing between knots.
items.fix: Pull each knot to the same tension, stopping as soon as the bead forms on the surface. Mark the knot positions along the drawn line before starting so the spacing is fixed.

items.symptom: The foundation thread puckers or pulls the fabric
items.cause: The foundation thread was laid with too much tension, or the fabric is not held taut in a hoop.
items.fix: Lay the foundation thread loosely along the line. The knots will hold it in place; it does not need to be pulled tight. Ensure the fabric is drum-taut in the hoop.
